links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 7, Dictionaries and Structuring Data
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: dictionaries, the birthdays and characterCount programs, the chessboard and the picnic.

links.title: Built-in Types (mapping types and dictionary views)
links.why: Every dictionary method and operator, insertion order, the views, and what __missing__ is.

links.title: 5. Data Structures (dictionaries and looping techniques)
links.why: The tutorial's account of dictionaries, dict comprehensions and looping over items().

links.title: collections - Container datatypes
links.why: Counter, defaultdict, OrderedDict and ChainMap, with worked examples of counting and grouping.

links.title: pprint - Data pretty printer
links.why: The answer to practice question 8, and the difference between pprint.pprint and pprint.pp.

links.title: copy - Shallow and deep copy operations
links.why: Why copying a nested dictionary needs deepcopy.

links.title: 3. Data model (object.__hash__)
links.why: The rule behind unhashable keys: what a hash must do and when a class is unhashable.

links.title: typing - Support for type hints (TypedDict)
links.why: TypedDict: a dictionary whose keys and value types a checker knows, and a plain dict at run time.

links.title: json - JSON encoder and decoder
links.why: How a nested dictionary becomes text and which keys json accepts.

links.title: PEP 584 - Add Union Operators To dict
links.why: Why dict got | and |=, and what they do with shared keys.

links.title: PEP 274 - Dict Comprehensions
links.why: The dictionary comprehension and how it came to Python 2.7 and 3.0.

links.title: PEP 634 - Structural Pattern Matching: Specification
links.why: The mapping pattern: how a match statement takes a dictionary apart by its keys.

links.title: PEP 589 - TypedDict: Type Hints for Dictionaries with a Fixed Set of Keys
links.why: The design of TypedDict for records with a fixed set of string keys.
